column1: # Laws allowed to be registered something other than `public`.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. A law's `privacy` column in science_law_registry.tsv
# decides whether a skip is legitimate. `public` means the inputs are tracked,
# so a skip is a failure and the law is enforced on every runner.
# `private-ok` and `derived-ok` both make a skip legal -- which converts an
# enforced law into one that no runner evaluates.
# That downgrade is a one-word edit to a TSV. ci_law_coverage.R counted and
# named the result but never failed on it, so the number could grow while the
# gate stayed green and merely printed a bigger total. The registry's own
# comment records this happening: registering L5 `private-ok` asserted that a
# 31 MB derived isochrone surface was person-level data.
# THIS LIST MAY ONLY SHRINK. A law that is non-public and not declared here
# fails coverage. A law declared here that has since become `public` must be
# deleted from this file -- a declaration must not outlive its cause, the same
# rule N1 enforces on ci_nightly_exceptions.txt and the CMS defect registry.
# Currently EMPTY, and that is the state worth defending: all 13 declared laws
# are `public`, so every one of them is enforced on every runner.
